plain_summary: A woman broke her arm on a nightclub dance floor and sued the tenant, only discovering years later that the landlord was involved in the nightclub's renovations. The court dismissed the landlord's appeal, ruling that the lawsuit was filed on time because the claim against the landlord was not discoverable until the tenant's discovery exam. This case matters for injury law because an injured person is not automatically required to sue a property landlord immediately if the landlord's involvement is not obvious.
